Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Consistent findings from transcript:
  - Acute asthma exacerbation in a patient with known asthma and atopy (eczema, hay fever) presenting with wheeze, shortness of breath, and cough; suboptimal relief with albuterol; recent onset over 2–3 days; baseline peak flow previously ~380.
  - Shared plan to escalate controller therapy and adjust short-acting relief accordingly; arrange timely follow-up.
  - Examination and peak flow will be performed to guide management; potential for antibiotics or systemic steroids if indicated by exam findings.
- Differential diagnoses (from DDx, aligned with transcript):
  - Acute asthma exacerbation (High)
  - Viral/URTI-triggered bronchospasm with asthma (Moderate)
  - Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction with underlying atopy/asthma (Moderate)
  - Allergic airway inflammation/Atopy-driven asthma (Moderate)
  - Other causes (e.g., anemia, neoplasm, PE) not supported by transcript (Low or not aligned)

Management Plan
- Main actions:
  - Albuterol (blue inhaler) use: continue as needed; consider limiting to every 2–4 hours; if uses that often, asthma is not well controlled
  - Beclomethasone (brown inhaler) dose: increase to 4 puffs twice daily during exacerbation; continue daily as maintenance
  - Monitor symptoms; if breathing worsens or cannot manage at home, seek urgent care (A&E)
  - Scheduling: referral for a GP asthma review in the next few days; chest examination and peak flow assessment planned at visit
  - Possible need for antibiotics or systemic steroids if exam findings suggest infection or persistence despite therapy

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Acute asthma exacerbation — High: Alignment with known asthma, current wheeze/SOB, insufficient relief with SABA, plan to escalate ICS and assess with peak flow.
- Viral/URTI-triggered bronchospasm with asthma — Moderate: Onset over several days with cough and dyspnea; atopy supports virus-driven bronchospasm.
- Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction with underlying atopy/asthma — Moderate: Triggered by running; current symptoms persist beyond exercise, suggesting broader exacerbation.
- Allergic airway inflammation/Atopy-driven asthma — Moderate: Atopy history (hay fever, eczema) and family history of asthma; ongoing ICS use with symptoms.
